title: Ticket Editor
description: Replace the read-only ticket details panel with an editable workspace, allowing engineers to modify ticket metadata without editing JSON files directly.
acceptanceCriteria: Ticket fields can be edited in-place.
Changes are validated before saving.
Unsaved changes are visually indicated.
Save and Cancel actions are provided.
The editor integrates with the existing ticket selection workflow.

title: Ticket Persistence
description: Implement the persistence layer for ticket data, allowing changes made in the Ticket Editor to be saved and reloaded without manual modification of the underlying JSON files.
acceptanceCriteria: Ticket changes can be saved.
Saved changes persist after application reload.
The persistence layer is reusable by future editors.
Save failures are handled gracefully.
The UI reflects successful saves.

title: Create Ticket
description: Implement the ability to create new tickets directly from the Foundry interface. New tickets should be initialised with sensible defaults, automatically assigned the next available ticket number, and persisted using the ticket persistence layer.
acceptanceCriteria: A user can create a new ticket from the Tickets workspace.
The next available FND ticket number is automatically assigned.
Default values are populated for required fields.
The new ticket is immediately selectable after creation.
The ticket is persisted successfully.

title: Delete Ticket
description: Allow engineers to permanently delete tickets from the project while preventing accidental data loss through a confirmation workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: A selected ticket can be deleted.
The user must confirm deletion before the ticket is removed.
The ticket is removed from persistence.
The ticket list refreshes automatically.
The next appropriate ticket is automatically selected.
Deleting the final ticket leaves the workspace in a valid empty state.

title: Ticket Validation
description: Implement client-side validation for ticket creation and editing to ensure all ticket data is complete, consistent and conforms to the Foundry data model before it can be saved.
acceptanceCriteria: Required fields are validated before saving.
Invalid tickets cannot be saved.
Users receive clear feedback when validation fails.
Validation rules are shared between Create and Edit workflows.
Validation logic is encapsulated in a reusable validator.

title: Reusable Validation Rendering
description: Implement a reusable validation framework for Foundry editors, providing inline validation, field state tracking and a consistent user experience across tickets, projects, milestones and releases.
acceptanceCriteria: Validation renderer component created.
Inline validation messages displayed.
Invalid fields visually highlighted.
Previous validation errors cleared before each validation.
Ticket editor uses the reusable renderer.

title: Project Editor
description: Allow project configuration to be edited from within Foundry rather than directly editing JSON files.
acceptanceCriteria: Project metadata can be edited.
Current sprint can be updated.
Current release can be updated.
Project changes are validated before saving.
Changes are persisted through the backend API.

title: Milestone Editor
description: Provide full milestone management within Foundry.
acceptanceCriteria: Milestones can be created.
Milestones can be edited.
Milestones can be deleted.
Milestones are validated before saving.
Milestone changes are persisted through the backend API.

title: Release Editor
description: Provide full release management within Foundry.
acceptanceCriteria: Releases can be created.
Releases can be edited.
Releases can be deleted.
Releases are validated before saving.
Release changes are persisted through the backend API.

title: Ticket Relationships
description: Support relationships between tickets to model dependencies and related work.
acceptanceCriteria: Tickets can be marked as blocked by another ticket.
Tickets can be marked as depending on another ticket.
Related tickets can be linked.
Circular dependencies are prevented.
Relationship information is displayed within the ticket editor.

title: Search & Filtering
description: Improve ticket discovery through searching and filtering.
acceptanceCriteria: Tickets can be searched by ID.
Tickets can be searched by title.
Tickets can be filtered by status.
Tickets can be filtered by priority.
Multiple filters can be combined.
Results update without reloading the page.

title: Ticket Sorting
description: Allow tickets to be sorted using multiple criteria.
acceptanceCriteria: Tickets can be sorted by ID.
Tickets can be sorted by priority.
Tickets can be sorted by status.
Tickets can be sorted by milestone.
Manual ordering remains available.

title: Workspace Persistence
description: Persist the user's current working context independently of project configuration so Foundry restores the previous workspace on startup.
acceptanceCriteria: The active project is restored when Foundry starts.
The selected ticket is restored when Foundry starts.
The selected milestone is restored when Foundry starts.
The selected release is restored when Foundry starts.
Workspace state is stored separately from project configuration.
Project configuration no longer contains transient UI state.
notes: Introduce a dedicated workspace model (for example workspace.json) to separate persistent application state from project metadata. This lays the foundation for future user preferences, multiple workspaces and session restoration.

title: Partial View Rendering
description: Refactor the ticket workspace to support partial UI updates without re-rendering the entire page, improving responsiveness and preserving focus during interactive operations.
acceptanceCriteria: Updating the ticket list does not recreate the editor.
Updating search results preserves focus in the search box.
Ticket selection is preserved where possible.
Search, filtering and sorting update only the ticket list.
Partial rendering utilities are reusable by future views.
